title: Pulpal Reaction to Caries & Operative Procedures — Test

mcqs.q: Pulp injury is described as:
mcqs.explain: Because many factors contribute, every effort should be taken to minimize pulpal injuries at each stage.

mcqs.q: In restorative procedures, the pulp is subjected to injury:
opts: Before, during and after restoration of the tooth
Only after the restoration is placed
Only when the preparation approaches the pulp horn
mcqs.explain: Caries injures it before, cutting injures it during, and the material and oral conditions injure it after.

mcqs.q: The three categories of pulpal irritant are:
mcqs.explain: Physical irritation is also called mechanical, and microbial irritation is also called biological.

mcqs.q: The source of microbial (biological) irritation is:
mcqs.explain: The other three are chemical or physical irritants.

mcqs.q: Which pair represents CORONAL spread of bacteria to the pulp?
mcqs.explain: Root caries and retrograde infection are the two routes of radicular spread.

mcqs.q: Retrograde infection is a route of:
mcqs.explain: It reaches the pulp through the root, alongside root caries.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a cause of physical (mechanical) irritation?
mcqs.explain: Setting by-products are chemical irritants; trauma is the fourth physical cause.

mcqs.q: During cavity preparation, the pulp is injured by heat generation, desiccation and:
mcqs.explain: These three — thermal, vibrational and desiccating — are the injuries of the cutting itself.

mcqs.q: Chemical irritation during insertion of a restorative material is caused by:
opts: Chemicals and the reaction by-products generated during setting
Mechanical vibration from the condensing instrument
The temperature of the material as it is carried to the tooth
mcqs.explain: After placement, the effect is instead influenced by the oral conditions.

mcqs.q: The three pulpal responses to irritants are tubular sclerosis, pulpal inflammation and:
opts: Calcific metamorphosis of the root canal
mcqs.explain: The first two are protective; inflammation is the response once the insult exceeds them.

mcqs.q: Reactionary dentin is formed when:
opts: The injury is MILD and the primary odontoblasts SURVIVE
The injury is severe and the primary odontoblasts are destroyed
The dentinal tubules have been sealed by a restoration
mcqs.explain: The surviving odontoblasts are stimulated to synthesize it; if they are damaged, reparative dentin is formed instead.

mcqs.q: Tubular sclerosis is a process in which:
opts: Mineral is deposited within the dentinal tubules, reducing the permeability of the dentin
A new layer of dentin is laid down at the pulp–dentin interface
The odontoblastic processes retract from the tubules
Collagen is deposited in the intertubular matrix
mcqs.explain: The sclerosed dentin becomes impermeable to bacteria and toxic products.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT another name for tubular sclerosis?
mcqs.explain: Reparative dentin is the separate, tertiary response formed when the primary odontoblasts are damaged.

mcqs.q: Reparative (tertiary) dentin is formed:
opts: At the interface between dentin and pulp, when the primary odontoblasts are damaged
Within the dentinal tubules, when the odontoblasts survive
Throughout the whole pulp chamber uniformly
mcqs.explain: Its distribution is limited to the area beneath the stimulus.

mcqs.q: The distribution of reparative dentin is:
opts: Limited to the area beneath the stimulus
Spread uniformly around the whole pulp chamber
Confined to the floor of the pulp chamber
mcqs.explain: The response is localised to where the irritant reaches the pulp.

mcqs.q: MORE reparative dentin is formed in response to:
mcqs.explain: The rate of reparative dentin formation is related to the rate of carious attack — a slow attack gives the pulp time to respond.

mcqs.q: What is the relationship between RPM and heat production?
opts: The more the RPM, the more the heat production
The more the RPM, the less the heat production
RPM has no effect on heat production
Heat production peaks at medium RPM
mcqs.explain: Whenever the RPMs are increased, pressure must be correspondingly reduced.

mcqs.q: Pressure applied during cutting is:
opts: Related only to the surface area of contact
mcqs.explain: This is why increased speed must be paired with reduced pressure.

mcqs.q: The surface area of contact is related to:
opts: The size and shape of the revolving tool
The hardness of the tooth structure
mcqs.explain: The more the contact between tooth structure and revolving tool, the more the heat generation.

mcqs.q: As the remaining dentin thickness DECREASES, the pulpal insult from heat or desiccation:
mcqs.explain: Enamel and dentin are good thermal insulators — less tissue means less insulation.

mcqs.q: A MILD injury produces:
opts: A localized protective pulpal response in the region of the cut tubules — reactionary dentin
A localized protective response — reparative dentin
A destructive response extending beyond the cut tubules
mcqs.explain: A moderate injury gives reparative dentin; a severe one gives a destructive response.

mcqs.q: A SEVERE injury produces:
opts: A destructive response spreading beyond the cut tubules, with abscess and necrosis
Tubular sclerosis of the dentin only
mcqs.explain: The key distinction is that the response is no longer confined to the region of the cut tubules.

mcqs.q: How long should one wait to observe the pulpal effects of a MILD TO MODERATE injury?
mcqs.explain: That is the period in which reactionary or reparative dentin becomes apparent.

mcqs.q: How long should one wait to observe the pulpal effects of a SEVERE injury?
mcqs.explain: Necrosis or death of the pulp may take that long to declare itself.

mcqs.q: A YOUNG pulp, compared with an older pulp, is:
opts: More prone to injury but recovers better — large chamber, rich blood supply
Less prone to injury and recovers more effectively than an older pulp
More prone to injury and recovers less effectively than an older pulp
Equally prone to injury but recovers less effectively
mcqs.explain: The large chamber brings the pulp closer to the insult, but the rich blood supply drives the repair.

mcqs.q: According to Marzouck, a remaining dentin thickness of 2 mm or greater gives:
mcqs.explain: 0.8–2 mm gives an unhealthy reparative response, and 0.3–0.8 mm a destructive one.

mcqs.q: According to Marzouck, a DESTRUCTIVE pulpal response occurs at an RDT of:
mcqs.explain: Below 0.8 mm there is too little insulating dentin left to protect the pulp.

mcqs.q: An RDT of 1.5 mm falls into which of Marzouck's bands?
mcqs.explain: It is above the destructive threshold of 0.8 mm but below the healthy threshold of 2 mm.

mcqs.q: The rise in temperature during cutting should not be greater than:
mcqs.explain: The longer the time of cutting and the higher the local temperature, the greater the threat of thermal trauma.

mcqs.q: Why do STEEL burs produce more heat than carbide burs?
opts: Because of inefficient cutting when used without coolants
Because steel conducts heat better than carbide
Because they are always used at higher RPM
Because they have a larger surface area of contact
mcqs.explain: Inefficient cutting means more friction for the same amount of tooth removed.

mcqs.q: Compared with carbide burs, diamond rotary cutting points generate:
mcqs.explain: The abrasive particles cut by grinding, which is more frictional than the shearing of a bladed bur.

mcqs.q: Heat during cutting is fundamentally produced by:
opts: Chemical reaction at the tooth surface
mcqs.explain: This is why dull or debris-plugged instruments, which cut inefficiently, produce the most heat.

mcqs.q: Burs and diamond instruments that are dull or plugged with debris:
opts: Do not cut efficiently, resulting in heat production
Cut more slowly but more safely
Produce less heat because they remove less tooth structure
Should be used with air coolant only
mcqs.explain: Efficiency and pulpal safety go together — a sharp instrument is a safe instrument.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a means of reducing heat production?
opts: Using a proper handpiece without vibration
mcqs.explain: Pressure is directly proportional to heat generation, so increasing it makes matters worse.

mcqs.q: Air alone as a coolant is ineffective in preventing pulpal damage because:
opts: It desiccates the dentin and damages the odontoblasts
It is too cold for the pulp
It cannot be delivered at high speed
It washes away the smear layer
mcqs.explain: Air also has a much lower heat dissipation capacity than water.

mcqs.q: Compared with water, air has:
opts: A much lower heat dissipation capacity, and is much less efficient in absorbing unwanted heat
A higher heat dissipation capacity but poorer visibility
A higher capacity only at high flow rates
mcqs.explain: In addition, the dentin powder gets clogged in the blade, reducing efficiency further.

mcqs.q: Air alone as a coolant may be used:
opts: Only when visibility is a problem, such as during finishing and polishing
mcqs.explain: It is combined with low speed and light intermittent pressure application.

mcqs.q: When air alone is used as a coolant, it must be combined with:
opts: Low speed and light intermittent pressure
High speed and firm continuous pressure
High speed and light continuous pressure
Low speed and firm continuous pressure
mcqs.explain: The advantages are that visibility will not be affected and trauma is minimized.

mcqs.q: The air–water spray lubricates, cleans and cools the cutting instrument, thereby:
opts: Increasing its efficiency and service life
Reducing the need for local anaesthesia
Allowing higher pressure to be used safely
mcqs.explain: It also cools, moistens and clears the operating site and the burs during normal cutting procedures.

mcqs.q: The main DISADVANTAGE of the in-built water spray of modern handpieces is that it:
opts: Prevents proper vision of the operating area
Is only available on high-speed handpieces
mcqs.explain: It is present on both high-speed and low-speed handpieces; the nurse's continuous spray and suction overcome the vision problem.

mcqs.q: The smear layer is:
opts: A layer of debris formed during cutting that covers the cut surface of enamel and dentin
A mineralised layer deposited by the odontoblasts
A film of saliva on the prepared surface
The outermost layer of the restorative material
mcqs.explain: It is produced by the cutting itself, not by the tooth or the restoration.

mcqs.q: The smear layer on dentin is described as:
opts: Entirely harmful and always to be removed
mcqs.explain: It occludes tubules and inhibits fluid flow and microleakage, but its porosity limits the protection.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a protective action of the smear layer?
opts: It inhibits the outward flow of tubular fluid
It inhibits inward penetration of microleakage contamination
mcqs.explain: Its protection is purely physical — an occlusive barrier, not a chemical one.

mcqs.q: When air is applied to a prepared cavity, local desiccation may:
opts: Produce fluid flow and affect the physiologic status of the odontoblastic processes
Harden the smear layer and improve sealing
mcqs.explain: Rapid outward fluid flow draws the odontoblast nuclei into the tubules and can kill the cells.

mcqs.q: The correct endpoint for drying a preparation with air is:
opts: A glistening surface — removing excess moisture only, not over-drying
A chalky white, completely dry surface
A surface dried for at least 10 seconds
mcqs.explain: Over-drying is precisely what causes the damaging fluid flow.

mcqs.q: Restorative materials should ideally be:
opts: Biocompatible with the pulp, and have a therapeutic effect on the pulp as well
Biocompatible only, with no biological activity
Cytotoxic enough to sterilise the cavity
mcqs.explain: Calcium hydroxide is the material that best meets the therapeutic half of this requirement.

mcqs.q: Which cement is the MOST IRRITATING to the pulp?
mcqs.explain: It causes severe pulpal irritation, and ideally should not be used as a base or temporary restoration.

mcqs.q: Why is zinc phosphate cement so irritating?
opts: Its liquid is phosphoric acid, with a pH of about 1
It generates a large exothermic reaction on setting
Its particles penetrate the dentinal tubules
mcqs.explain: That extreme acidity is transmitted through the dentinal tubules to the pulp.

mcqs.q: Zinc polycarboxylate cement causes only MILD pulpal irritation because:
opts: Its polyacrylic acid is co-polymerized, leaving no free acid radicals
It contains calcium hydroxide as an internal buffer
Its liquid is distilled water rather than an acid
It sets so quickly the acid has no time to diffuse
mcqs.explain: It can therefore be used as a base material and as a temporary filling material.

mcqs.q: Which material has the MOST THERAPEUTIC action on the pulp?
mcqs.explain: It is antimicrobial, highly alkaline, and promotes reparative dentin formation.

mcqs.q: The alkalinity of calcium hydroxide cement is approximately:
mcqs.explain: That alkalinity is responsible for the pulp therapy and for its antimicrobial action.

mcqs.q: Calcium hydroxide helps in reparative dentin formation, producing a:
mcqs.explain: The bridge walls off the exposure with newly formed hard tissue.

mcqs.q: Why can the polyacrylic acid of glass ionomer cement not irritate the pulp through the tubules?
opts: Its molecular weight is larger than the diameter of the dentinal tubule
It is neutralised instantly on contact with dentin
It is not acidic at all
The smear layer always blocks it completely
mcqs.explain: The molecule physically cannot enter the tubule, so it cannot reach the pulp.

mcqs.q: Which property of glass ionomer cement is NOT listed?
opts: A liquid molecule larger than the tubule diameter
mcqs.explain: The lecture's reasons for its biocompatibility are adhesion, molecular size and anticariogenicity.

mcqs.q: Amalgam is considered a SELF-SEALING material because:
opts: Corrosion products such as silver and copper oxide seal the microleakage space
It expands continuously throughout its service life
It releases fluoride that remineralises the margins
mcqs.explain: This is why the marginal seal of an amalgam improves rather than deteriorates with time.

mcqs.q: In a DEEP cavity to be restored with composite resin, it is advisable to:
opts: Use a GIC base and then restore
Etch for twice as long to improve the bond
Place a zinc phosphate base first
mcqs.explain: The acid etching in a deep cavity may irritate the pulp; the GIC base intervenes between the etch and the pulp.

mcqs.q: Which is a CHEMICAL factor influencing the effect of a restorative material on the pulp?
opts: Absorption of water from dentin during setting
mcqs.explain: Heat and marginal adaptation are physical; cytotoxicity is biological.

mcqs.q: Poor marginal adaptation of a restoration is classified as which kind of factor?
opts: Physical — it leads to bacterial penetration
Chemical — it allows acid to reach the pulp
Biological — it is a form of cytotoxicity
mcqs.explain: The consequence is biological, but the factor itself is a physical defect in the restoration.

mcqs.q: Cytotoxicity of a restorative material is classified as a:
mcqs.explain: The chemical factors are acidity/pH and water absorption; the physical are setting heat and marginal adaptation.

saqs.q: List the pulpal irritants under their three headings, with examples.
saqs.a: MICROBIAL — the carious lesion, coronal spread (caries, crown fracture) and radicular spread (root caries, retrograde infection). PHYSICAL — operative procedures, trauma, orthodontic movement, deep curettage; during preparation heat, vibration and desiccation. CHEMICAL — reaction by-products during setting, and oral conditions after placement.

head: Heading
Examples
rows: the carious lesion — coronal spread of bacteria (dental caries, crown fracture) and radicular spread (root caries, retrograde infection)
operative procedures · trauma · orthodontic movement · deep periodontal curettage. During cavity preparation: heat (thermal), mechanical vibration (pressure) and desiccation
during insertion of the restorative material — chemicals and reaction by-products generated during setting; and after placement, influenced by oral conditions

saqs.q: Describe the three pulpal responses to irritants.
saqs.a: TUBULAR SCLEROSIS — mild injury, primary odontoblasts survive and lay reactionary dentin; mineral in the tubules reduces permeability. TERTIARY/REPARATIVE DENTIN — formed at the dentin–pulp interface when primary odontoblasts are damaged, limited to the area beneath the stimulus. PULPAL INFLAMMATION.

head: Response
What happens
rows: injury is mild and the primary odontoblasts survive, being stimulated to synthesize reactionary dentin (intertubular / sclerotic dentin). Mineral is deposited within the tubules, reducing permeability and making dentin impermeable to bacteria and toxic products
a layer formed at the interface between dentin and pulp when the primary odontoblasts are damaged; distribution limited to the area beneath the stimulus

saqs.q: Distinguish reactionary from reparative dentin, and state what determines the rate of reparative dentin formation.
saqs.a: REACTIONARY — mild injury, PRIMARY ODONTOBLASTS SURVIVE; mineral laid within the tubules. REPARATIVE — at the dentin–pulp interface when PRIMARY ODONTOBLASTS ARE DAMAGED, limited to beneath the stimulus. Rate relates to the rate of carious attack: MORE reparative dentin forms against slow, inactive caries than against active caries.

head: REACTIONARY
REPARATIVE
rows: injury is mild — the PRIMARY ODONTOBLASTS SURVIVE and are stimulated
mineral is laid down within the tubules themselves
forms at the interface between dentin and pulp, limited to the area beneath the stimulus

ans.text: The rate of reparative dentin formation is related to the rate of carious attack — MORE is formed in response to slow, inactive caries than to active caries.

saqs.q: List the factors in restorative procedures that influence the effect on the pulp.
saqs.a: Rotary cutting — heat (RPM, pressure, surface area of contact, RDT, absence of coolants), mechanical vibration and desiccation; cavity depth / RDT; time of cutting; types of burs; nature of the cutting instrument; use of coolants; and the smear layer.

list: Use of rotary cutting instruments — heat production (governed by RPM, pressure, surface area of contact, RDT and absence of coolants), mechanical vibration and desiccation
Cavity effective depth or RDT (remaining dentin thickness)
Time of cutting
Types of burs
Nature of the cutting instrument
Use of instrument coolants
The smear layer

saqs.q: Explain how RPM, pressure and surface area of contact each affect heat production.
saqs.a: RPM — more RPM, more heat. PRESSURE — directly proportional to heat; when RPM rises, pressure must be reduced. SURFACE AREA OF CONTACT — related to the size and shape of the tool; more contact, more heat.

head: Factor
Effect on heat
rows: the more the RPM, the more the heat production
directly proportional to heat generation — whenever RPM is increased, pressure must be correspondingly reduced
related to the size and shape of the revolving tool — the more contact between tooth and tool, the more heat

saqs.q: Tabulate the type of injury against its effect on the pulp.
saqs.a: MILD — localized protective response at the cut tubules: REACTIONARY dentin. MODERATE — localized protective response at the cut tubules: REPARATIVE dentin. SEVERE — destructive response extending BEYOND the cut tubules: pulpal abscess and necrosis.

head: Injury
Effect on the pulp
rows: a localized protective response in the region of the cut dentinal tubules — REACTIONARY dentin
a localized protective response in the region of the cut dentinal tubules — REPARATIVE dentin
a destructive response extending BEYOND the cut tubules — pulpal abscess and death/necrosis of the pulp

saqs.q: State the time periods over which pulpal effects should be observed, and comment on the age of the pulp.
saqs.a: MILD TO MODERATE — 2 weeks, for reactionary or reparative dentin. SEVERE — 6 months or longer, for necrosis. A young pulp is more prone to injury but recovers more effectively, because of its large chamber and rich blood supply.

head: Injury
Observe over
rows: 2 weeks — for reactionary or reparative dentin
6 months or longer — for necrosis or death of the pulp

ans.text: Although a young pulp is more prone to injury, it also recovers more effectively than an older pulp, because of its large chamber and rich blood supply.

saqs.q: Explain the importance of remaining dentin thickness, and give Marzouck's classification.
saqs.a: Enamel and dentin are good thermal insulators and protect the pulp when thickness is adequate; as RDT decreases, injury increases. MARZOUCK: ≥2 mm — healthy reparative response; 0.8–2 mm — unhealthy reparative response; 0.3–0.8 mm — destructive response.

ans.text: Enamel and dentin are good thermal insulators and protect the pulp when the remaining thickness is adequate and less heat is generated. As the RDT decreases, pulpal injury increases.

saqs.q: Discuss the effect of bur type and bur condition on heat production.
saqs.a: Steel burs produce more heat than carbide because they cut inefficiently without coolants. Diamond points generate more damaging heat than carbide. Heat comes fundamentally from FRICTION, and dull or debris-plugged instruments cut inefficiently and so produce heat.

head: Instrument
Heat
rows: produce more heat than carbide — inefficient cutting when used without coolants
generate more damaging heat than carbide burs

ans.text: Heat is produced fundamentally because of FRICTION — burs and diamonds that are dull or plugged with debris do not cut efficiently, and so produce heat.

saqs.q: Why is air alone an inadequate coolant, and when may it legitimately be used?
saqs.a: Air alone desiccates dentin and damages odontoblasts, has much lower heat-dissipation capacity than water, and lets dentin powder clog the blade. Use it ONLY when visibility is a problem — finishing and polishing — with low speed and light intermittent pressure; visibility is preserved and trauma minimized.

list: It desiccates the dentin and damages the odontoblasts
Much lower heat dissipation capacity than water, so far less efficient at absorbing unwanted heat
Dentin powder clogs the blade, reducing cutting efficiency

ans.text: It may be used ONLY when visibility is a problem — during finishing and polishing of the preparation and restorations — combined with low speed and light intermittent pressure. The advantages are that visibility is not affected and trauma is minimized.

saqs.q: Give the advantages of the air–water spray and the disadvantage of the in-built spray.
saqs.a: ADVANTAGES — universally used; cools, moistens and clears the site and the burs; lubricates, cleans and cools the instrument, increasing efficiency and service life. DISADVANTAGE of the in-built spray — it prevents proper vision of the operating area, so the nurse provides water spray continuously.

list: Universally used
Cools, moistens and clears the operating site and the burs during normal cutting
Lubricates, cleans and cools the cutting instrument, increasing its efficiency and service life

ans.text: Disadvantage of the in-built spray — in current handpieces, high and low speed alike, the in-built spray prevents proper vision of the operating area. To overcome this, the dental nurse provides water spray continuously.

saqs.q: What is the smear layer, and in what way is it protective?
saqs.a: A layer of debris covering the cut enamel and dentin. It is MODERATELY protective — it occludes the tubules, inhibits outward flow of tubular fluid and inhibits inward penetration of microleakage contamination. But it is still POROUS, so protection is only partial.

ans.text: In cutting procedures a layer of debris forms covering the cut surface of enamel and dentin.

list: Occludes the dentinal tubules
Inhibits the outward flow of tubular fluid
Inhibits the inward penetration of microleakage contamination

ans.text: However it remains POROUS, so the protection it gives is only partial.

saqs.q: What happens if a preparation is over-dried with air, and what is the correct endpoint?
saqs.a: Local desiccation may produce fluid flow and affect the physiologic status of the odontoblastic processes. Apply air only to remove excess moisture, leaving a GLISTENING surface — not an over-dried one.

ans.text: Local desiccation may produce fluid flow and affect the physiologic status of the odontoblastic processes of the underlying dentin. Air should be applied only to the extent of removing excess moisture, leaving a GLISTENING surface — not an over-dried one.

saqs.q: Compare zinc phosphate and zinc polycarboxylate cements with respect to pulpal irritation.
saqs.a: ZINC PHOSPHATE — the most irritating cement, SEVERE irritation; ideally not used as a base or temporary, since its liquid is phosphoric acid (pH 1). ZINC POLYCARBOXYLATE — only MILD irritation, usable as a base and temporary filling, since the polyacrylic acid is co-polymerized with mild acids and has chemical adhesion, leaving no free acid radicals.

head: ZINC PHOSPHATE
ZINC POLYCARBOXYLATE
rows: ideally not used as a base or temporary restoration
can be used as a base and as a temporary filling
its liquid is phosphoric acid, very acidic (pH 1)
the polyacrylic acid is co-polymerized with other mild acids, and it has chemical adhesion — no free acid radicals are left

saqs.q: Why is calcium hydroxide described as the most pulp-friendly material?
saqs.a: It has the most therapeutic action on the pulp: an antimicrobial action; alkalinity of about 11.6, responsible for the pulp therapy; and it helps reparative dentin formation, producing the calcific dentin bridge.

list: It has an antimicrobial action
Its alkalinity is about 11.6, which is responsible for the pulp therapy
It helps in reparative dentin formation, producing the calcific dentin bridge

saqs.q: Why is glass ionomer cement the most widely used material?
saqs.a: Because of its biocompatibility: it has an adhesion property; the molecular weight of the liquid polyacrylic acid is larger than the diameter of the dentinal tubule, so the acid cannot enter the tubules and reach the pulp; and it is anticariogenic.

list: It has an adhesion property
The molecular weight of the liquid polyacrylic acid is larger than the diameter of the dentinal tubule, so the acid cannot enter the tubules and reach the pulp
It has an anticariogenic property

saqs.q: Why is amalgam described as self-sealing, and what precaution applies to composite resin in a deep cavity?
saqs.a: AMALGAM is self-sealing because its corrosion products (silver and copper oxide) seal the microleakage space. COMPOSITE RESIN is the best direct esthetic material, but acid etching in a deep cavity may irritate the pulp — so use a GIC base first, then restore.

rows: the most time-tested and popular permanent restorative material; self-sealing because its corrosion products (silver and copper oxide) seal the microleakage space
the best esthetic direct restorative material — but acid etching in a deep cavity may irritate the pulp, so in a deep cavity use a GIC base and then restore

saqs.q: Classify the factors influencing the effect of restorative materials on the pulp.
saqs.a: CHEMICAL — acidity/pH; absorption of water from dentin during setting. PHYSICAL — heat generated during setting; poor marginal adaptation leading to bacterial penetration. BIOLOGICAL — cytotoxicity of the material.

head: Factor
Detail
rows: acidity / pH · absorption of water from dentin during setting
heat generated during setting · poor marginal adaptation, leading to bacterial penetration
